proposed_widenings.name: ClassFeatureActivationCost.reaction
proposed_widenings.justification: The feature costs a Reaction to activate. ClassFeatureActivationCost currently only allows 'free' and 'bonus_action'. A reaction variant is needed, ideally carrying a ReactionTrigger (hit by attack with B/P/S damage).
proposed_widenings.evidence: you can take a Reaction to reduce the attack's total damage against you

proposed_widenings.name: reduce_damage_taken
proposed_widenings.justification: Phase 1 reduces incoming damage by a dice expression (1d10 + Dex modifier + Monk level). No existing ClassFeatureEffect covers numeric incoming-damage reduction. TAXONOMY v4 §12 explicitly lists this atom as deferred single-group pressure from 'class-feature reactions' — this unit is exactly that pressure.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The reduction equals 1d10 plus your Dexterity modifier and Monk level.

proposed_widenings.name: conditional_follow_up (damage_to_zero gate)
proposed_widenings.justification: Phase 2 fires only when Phase 1 reduces damage to exactly 0. No existing class feature family supports a conditional secondary phase gated on the result of Phase 1. The pattern requires: threshold gate (damage=0) → optional Focus Point expenditure → distance-conditional target selection (melee: 5ft / ranged: 60ft no total cover) → save_gate → outbound damage. This is structurally new.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you reduce the damage to 0, you can expend 1 Focus Point to redirect some of the attack's force.

proposed_widenings.name: resource: focus_point_expenditure
proposed_widenings.justification: Phase 2 costs 1 Focus Point from the monk's shared Focus Point pool. The surface's UseCountResource models a per-feature use_count with rest resets. Focus Points are a shared class-level pool (Monk's Focus, L2) with a separate refill cadence. A new resource variant is needed to model expenditure from a named shared pool rather than a local counter.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you can expend 1 Focus Point to redirect some of the attack's force

proposed_widenings.name: DamageType.inherited_from_trigger
proposed_widenings.justification: The redirected damage takes the same type as the triggering attack. DamageType is a closed enum of fixed values; there is no 'same as trigger' or runtime-inherited variant. Encoding this honestly requires either a new variant or a runtime-reference pattern.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The damage is the same type dealt by the attack.

notes: Phase 1 (reaction + damage reduction) is blocked by two surface gaps: missing 'reaction' activation cost and missing 'reduce_damage_taken' effect. Phase 2 (conditional redirect) forces structural_widening: it introduces a damage-threshold conditional gate, Focus Point pool expenditure, attack-kind-conditional range selection, and outbound save_gate damage — none of which exist in the class feature surface. Both phases are needed for an honest encoding; omitting Phase 2 would misrepresent the feature. The TAXONOMY v4 §12 explicitly names reduce_damage_taken as a known deferred atom from class-feature reaction pressure; this unit is that pressure.
